input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience exit from the Agreement or an individual Service Option Attachment on one month's notice at a calendar month end, which is better than the 60–90 day fallback ceiling, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right: its only Agreement-level termination right is for material breach (3.3) and its only unilateral exit is term-end non-renewal on 90 days' notice (3.2). The clause failed the fallback on one material term because the early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A were open-ended, so we cap them at three months' charges for the terminated Services, a basis that reaches all such charges rather than only recurring ones. We also state the convenience qualifier expressly on each termination branch instead of once at the end of the sentence, without altering the one-month notice, the calendar month-end effective date, the prerequisite-attachment carve-out or the §3.3 proviso barring IBM from recovering §3.4(b) charges after its own breach. Preferred remains unmet only on a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges and a flat 30-day anchor; both are noted, not redlined.

proposal.summary: Express convenience right on each termination branch; cap early termination charges at three months' charges
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We state expressly that Customer may terminate this Agreement, or any Service Option Attachment, for convenience (the qualifier now appears on each branch rather than only at the end of the sentence), and we cap the open-ended Attachment A early termination charges at three months' charges for the terminated Services, per our fallback position.
